question: Which additive interaction components must disappear or become orthogonal in input and output embeddings when a softmax model represents specified conditional-independence and factorization relations?

key_findings.claim: Any embedding on a finite Cartesian-product domain admits a unique inclusion-exclusion decomposition into pure interactions indexed by subsets of factors.
key_findings.evidence: Projection operators Q_I separate the constant, unary, pairwise, and higher-order components of an embedding w on Z_1 times through Z_k. An embedding with only unary terms is additively disentangled and its values occupy a Minkowski-sum or product-of-simplices-like geometry.

key_findings.claim: The central theorem gives a necessary-and-sufficient orthogonality dictionary between conditional independence and input-output embedding interactions.
key_findings.evidence: For a softmax conditional model with logits equal to the inner product of u(x) and v(y), Theorem 3 states that the defined conditional-independence relation holds exactly when every interaction pair crossing the relevant partition has zero inner product, with the output subset nonempty. This extends earlier output-only factorization results to relations involving both input and output factors.

key_findings.claim: Span assumptions turn cross-orthogonality into disappearance of whole interaction components.
key_findings.evidence: Proposition 4 shows that if the input embeddings span the representation space, an output conditional independence forces the corresponding output interactions to vanish for every x. Proposition 5 analogously links relative causal independence of input factors to orthogonality of input interactions against all output differences, and makes them vanish when those differences span the space.

key_findings.claim: Paired input-output factorization implies a block-diagonal pattern in first-order interactions and eliminates relevant higher-order cross terms.
key_findings.evidence: Under a factorization P(Y given X)=h(x) times the product over i of f_i(x_i,y_i), Proposition 6 requires higher interactions to be orthogonal and unary u_i and v_j components to be orthogonal when i differs from j. This supplies a geometric signature for aligned factors such as image attributes paired with text attributes.

key_findings.claim: A small language-model experiment shows emergence of the predicted orthogonality pattern when the data distribution has the matching factorization.
key_findings.evidence: A 2.7M-parameter GPT-mini with vocabulary size 10 is trained for 20,000 steps with batch size 512 on synthetic three-factor sequences. Token-aligned decomposability is already visible at initialization, a permuted semantic factorization develops the expected interaction structure during training, and a nonfactorized distribution does not preserve the initially aligned pattern.

key_findings.claim: The theory characterizes exact final-logit geometry but does not establish causal representation, identifiability in unused dimensions, or robust approximate structure.
key_findings.evidence: Softmax probabilities constrain only inner products and logit differences, so overparameterized nullspaces can contain arbitrary components. The strongest vanishing conclusions require span conditions that may fail, and the paper gives no error bounds or statistical tests relating approximate conditional independence in finite data to small interaction norms. Its own definition permits choosing a positive input marginal to realize the independence relation, which is weaker than an intervention-based causal claim.

key_findings.claim: The empirical scope is illustrative and cannot validate general training dynamics or interpretability usefulness.
key_findings.evidence: The experiment uses one tiny synthetic model and reports qualitative interaction curves without repeated seeds, uncertainty, numerical thresholds, or downstream interventions. The ST5-XL and analogy examples are conceptual illustrations. The authors explicitly limit the framework to finite product domains and final softmax embeddings and assume that the model accurately represents the target conditional distribution.

method.core_idea: Decompose factored-domain embeddings into pure subset interactions and translate probabilistic factorization of a softmax conditional distribution into exact orthogonality constraints between those interactions.
method.mechanism: Apply Möbius-style inclusion-exclusion projections to input embeddings u and output embeddings v. Expand the inner-product logit in the resulting interaction bases, compare it with a multiplicative factorization of the conditional probability, and use softmax invariances plus span conditions to prove which cross terms must be zero or which interaction vectors must vanish.
assumptions: Input and output spaces are known finite Cartesian products with complete factor labels.
The trained model's conditional probabilities accurately realize the distribution under analysis.
Conditional independence is exact rather than approximate or sampling-noisy.
Span or output-difference conditions hold when a result concludes that interaction vectors vanish.
Final softmax embedding geometry is an adequate proxy for the representation phenomenon of interest.

techniques.role: Uses subset-indexed projections to isolate constant, unary, pairwise, and higher-order embedding components.
Converts multiplicative probability relations into additive logit constraints.
Characterizes conditional independence through zero inner products between incompatible input and output interactions.
Upgrades orthogonality against all represented inputs or outputs to vector-level disappearance.
Checks whether predicted geometry tracks semantic factors rather than fixed token coordinates during training.

evaluations.setting: 2.7M-parameter GPT-mini trained on a three-factor synthetic distribution with z1 conditionally independent of z2 given z3
evaluations.metric: Qualitative norms and inner products of interaction components over 20,000 training steps
evaluations.result: The predicted orthogonality pattern appears and remains aligned with the probabilistic factors.
evaluations.baseline: Initialization and a nonfactorized synthetic distribution

evaluations.setting: Permuted mapping between semantic factors and token coordinates
evaluations.metric: Emergence of the correct decomposable interaction structure
evaluations.result: Geometry shifts toward the permuted semantic factorization rather than staying locked to the initialization-aligned token axes.

evaluations.setting: Analogies, PCFG derivations, and paired vision-language factors including an ST5-XL illustration
evaluations.metric: Qualitative consistency with theorem-predicted parallelograms and orthogonality
evaluations.result: Examples can be expressed naturally in the interaction dictionary, but no quantitative downstream improvement is measured.
evaluations.baseline: Conceptual noncompositional alternatives rather than controlled empirical baselines

limitations: The framework assumes finite, explicitly factored Cartesian-product domains.
It analyzes final softmax input and output embeddings rather than intermediate network representations.
Exact conditional independence has no supplied perturbation bound for real, approximately factored data.
Strong vector-vanishing statements depend on representation-span assumptions.
The empirical study is one tiny synthetic model without multi-seed statistics or downstream interventions.
The paper does not explain why gradient training selects one admissible geometric realization over another.
failure_modes: Missing Cartesian combinations make inclusion-exclusion components impossible or statistically unstable to estimate.
Approximate independence can coexist with a large unnormalized interaction norm under poorly conditioned embeddings.
A low interaction norm can arise from softmax gauge freedom or collapse rather than meaningful compositionality.
Nullspace interactions can look entangled while leaving every conditional probability unchanged.
A learned factor permutation may be mistaken for failure if evaluation assumes fixed semantic axes.
Causal language can overstate a relation defined through existence of a compatible observational marginal.
reusable_insights: Use inclusion-exclusion projections to separate main effects from higher-order representational interactions.
State span and gauge conditions explicitly before interpreting orthogonality as absence of information.
Test compositional geometry under semantic-factor permutations to separate learning from initialization artifacts.
Measure probability-factorization error alongside embedding geometry rather than treating either alone as validation.
Develop normalized, perturbation-stable interaction scores before applying exact theorems to noisy data.
open_questions: What quantitative bounds connect approximate conditional mutual information to normalized interaction geometry?
Which implicit biases of optimization select disentangled versus nullspace-entangled solutions?
Can the decomposition be estimated reliably with sparse observations of a huge Cartesian product?
How can the theory extend from final softmax embeddings to contextual intermediate representations?
Do low interaction scores predict controllable compositional generalization on real tasks?
Can observational relative independence be separated empirically from genuine intervention-stable causal structure?

competitive_landscape.title: Linear Spaces of Meanings: Compositional Structures in Vision-Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: The predecessor studies compositional subspaces and output-side factorization in vision-language models with more direct CLIP applications. The reviewed paper generalizes the algebra to arbitrary interaction subsets and mixed input-output conditional relations.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Origins of Linear Representations in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: concurrent theoretical account of linear concepts
competitive_landscape.difference: This work derives conditions under which latent variables and gradient descent promote linear concept representations and includes LLaMA-2 evidence. The reviewed paper offers a more general static necessary-and-sufficient conditional-independence dictionary but does not model training dynamics.

competitive_landscape.title: The Linear Representation Hypothesis and the Geometry of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Park and colleagues define linear representations through counterfactual causal semantics and a causal inner product, then study probes and steering. The reviewed work focuses on factor interactions in final softmax embeddings and uses a weaker observational relative-independence definition.

competitive_landscape.title: Concept Algebra for (Score-Based) Text-Controlled Generative Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Concept Algebra develops subspace operations for score-based generative models and demonstrates controllable image generation. The reviewed paper provides exact softmax factorization theorems but no comparable real-model intervention benchmark.

novelty_assessment: The main novelty is a clean, general interaction-decomposition theorem that unifies input factors, output factors, and paired conditional relations under one softmax geometry. It extends a direct predecessor rather than introducing the broader linear-representation hypothesis. The mathematical dictionary is strong under exact finite-domain assumptions; its use as an empirical or causal interpretability tool remains speculative because identifiability, approximation stability, and real-model validation are unresolved.
reviewer_notes: Read all 15 extracted pages, including definitions, projection construction, Theorem 3, Propositions 4-6, proofs at the level presented, all qualitative examples, synthetic training experiment, and stated limitations. Primary arXiv records were checked for the direct vision-language predecessor, two contemporaneous theories of linear representation, and Concept Algebra. The review flags the distinction between exact logit constraints and identifiable causal internal structure.
